# DAUDIT-3 (lane id daudit3-ci-generated-results): the committed design-audit results are generated by CI only, 2026-10-08

Branch `lane/daudit3-ci-generated-results`, cut from origin/master 910f35a75. Prior decision read: DAUDIT-2 (PR 1049) diffed the green CI run's artifact against the results.json it had committed from Windows: 4 rows differed (the `ch` width of the vendored font, a 44px target), both with 0 harness errors.

## Accomplished

- `fsi-app/.discipline/rendering/audit/run-audit.mjs`: one new function `generatedOn(env, proc)` returns `{ platform, node, container_image }` (container image from `AUDIT_CONTAINER_IMAGE`, which the workflow reads out of its own file, else `none`). results.json carries it as `generated_on`; `renderDocument` prints it as a "Generated on" line in the Repo state block, reading the same object. Confirmed by reading the file: one construction site.
- `fsi-app/.discipline/rendering/audit/generated-on.test.mjs` (new, node builtins only, discovered by the discipline suite): refuses a committed results.json or audit document whose platform is not linux, a missing stamp, a missing document line, and a document that disagrees with results.json. Runs the real `generatedOn` extracted from the generator source. Seven ATTACK tests (win32, darwin, no stamp, no document line, disagreement) pass.
- `.github/workflows/design-audit.yml`: new step "Commit the audit result back to the dispatched ref (workflow_dispatch only)", guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, placed after the summary step (so a harness-errored run never commits) and before the upload. It stages the audit document and calls the shared `fsi-app/scripts/maintenance/commit-worklist-artifact.sh` with the dispatched ref, which stages results.json, commits both as one commit as github-actions[bot], and degrades to a warning on `master` or on a rejected push. Job-level `permissions: contents: write` added (top level stays `contents: read`); the audit step reads the image from the workflow file and exports `AUDIT_CONTAINER_IMAGE`.
- `fsi-app/scripts/proof/design-audit-workflow.test.mjs`: the "no write permission" rule now permits exactly the job-level `contents: write` and refuses any other write; new commit-back rules (guard, shared script, ref, both files, order after the summary step and before the upload, no other step commits or pushes). Eight new attack tests (guard removed, guard flipped to pull_request, step dropped, a second unguarded push, an extra write permission or the job permission dropped, a hand-rolled push replacing the shared script, commit-back before the summary step) plus a test that runs the image-reading sed on the workflow text.
- `fsi-app/.discipline/rendering/audit/README.md`: new section "The committed results are CI's" (stamp, a local run is never committed, how to refresh by dispatching the workflow), step 5 of "Adding a part" no longer says to commit the regenerated document, Files table updated.

## Read and reused

Read: lane common terms and brief, CLAUDE.md, the lane contract's Write set and Wiring preflight sections, `.github/workflows/design-audit.yml`, `run-audit.mjs` (header, `renderDocument`, results writer), `design-audit-workflow.test.mjs`, `commit-worklist-artifact.sh` and `commit-brief-apply-artifact.sh`, the two call sites in `maintenance.yml`, the audit README. Finding: no workflow under `.github/workflows` contains `git commit` any more (STATUTORY-WRITER removed them); the only commit-back mechanism left is `commit-worklist-artifact.sh`, so the new step calls it rather than copying its push-degradation logic. The script takes one path, so the document is staged in the workflow first and results.json by the script: one commit.

## Red then green

- Static stamp test against the unmodified generator: 3 failures (committed files, `generatedOn` missing, construction-site check). With the generator change: 8 pass, 1 fails, and the one failure is the intended red (the committed Windows-generated results.json has no stamp) until the dispatched run commits the CI pair back.
- Workflow shape test against the unmodified workflow: 20 pass, 8 fail. Against the new workflow: 28 of 28.

## Decisions

- Job-level `contents: write` is the only way to give a single step push rights; the guard on the step keeps the pull_request path read-only in effect, and the shape test refuses any other write permission.
- A push with the workflow token does not start workflow runs, so the commit-back does not re-run the PR checks; the lane follows the pull with an ordinary push.

## NOT done

- No local run of the generator (no node_modules in the worktree, no browser); the stamp's behaviour in the generator is proven by extracting and running `generatedOn`, and end to end by the dispatched CI run (below). [NOT-WORK: COMMON rule 9, CI is the gate; proven by the dispatched run]
- Nothing in master is committed from a developer machine by this lane; results.json and the audit document are changed only by the CI commit-back. [NOT-WORK: fact, no action]

## CI-generated result and dispatch evidence (confirmed by reading the pulled files)

- PR 1057. First `gh workflow run design-audit.yml --ref lane/daudit3-ci-generated-results` (run 37876356793) committed the pair back as github-actions[bot] and stamped `container_image: none`: the `job.container.image` context value is not exposed. Fixed in the next commit (the audit step reads the image out of the workflow file with the install step's own sed and exports `AUDIT_CONTAINER_IMAGE`); second dispatch (run 37876599400) committed the pair again with `generated_on: { platform: "linux", node: "v24.21.0", container_image: "mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble" }`, and the audit document's Repo state block carries the matching "Generated on" line.
- Counts from the CI-generated file (identical in both CI runs): 73 specs, 2527 checks, 0 harness errors; MATCH 2455, MISMATCH 54, NOT BUILT 18, NOT IN SPEC 0. DAUDIT-2's Windows file read MATCH 2459, MISMATCH 51, NOT BUILT 17: the machine-dependent difference is 4 MATCH to non-matching plus 1 NOT BUILT shift (the ch width of the vendored font, a 44px target, and others), which is exactly why the committed oracle must be CI's. The new non-matching rows were not traced by this lane (out of scope; a follow-up review lane owns them).
- After the pull: `node --test` on `generated-on.test.mjs` and `design-audit-workflow.test.mjs`: 37 pass, 0 fail (the intended red is gone).
- The first CI run on the PR (before the dispatch) failed two jobs: the discipline suite on the intended red, and ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` on an unused `eslint-disable` directive in my own test (removed in the next commit).
- A push by the workflow token does not start workflow runs, so the lane's own follow-up push re-ran the PR checks.
